source_text: De sabbato quoque illud praemitto, nec hanc quaesti- onem consistere potuisse, si non deum sabbati circumferret Christus. nec enim disceptaretur, cur destrueret sabbatum, si destruere deberet. porro destruere deberet, si alterius dei esset, nec quisquam miraretur facientem quod illi congruebat. mirabantur ergo, quia non congruebat illi deum creatorem circumferre et sabbatum eius impugnare. et ut prima quaeque decidamus, ne eadem ubique nouemus ad omnem argumentationem aduersarii ex aliqua noua Christi institutione nitentem. haec iam definitio stabit: ideo de nouitate institutionis cuiusque disceptatum, quia de nouitate diuinitatis nihil erat usque adhuc editum, sicuti nec disceptatum ***, nec posse retorqueri ex ipsa nouitate institutionis cuiusque satis aliam a Christo demonstratam diuinitatem, quando et ipsam nouitatem pronuntiatam a creatore constiterit in Christo non esse mirandam et oportuerit utique prius alium deum exponi, postea disciplinam eius induci, quia deus auctoritatem praestet disciplinae, non deo disciplina; nisi si et Marcion plane tam peruersas non per magistrum litteras didicit, sed per litteras magistrum.
pass_a_gloss: Also about the Sabbath I premit this, and this question would not have been able to consist, if Christ were not carrying around the God of the Sabbath. For it would not have been disputed, why he was destroying the Sabbath, if he ought to destroy it. Further, he ought to destroy it, if it were of another God, and no one would wonder at him doing what was fitting to that one. They were wondering, therefore, because it was not fitting to him, to carry around the creating God and to attack his Sabbath. And so that we may decide each first thing, lest we notice the same things everywhere in every argumentation of the adversary leaning on some new institution of Christ. This definition will already stand: therefore it was disputed about the newness of each institution, because nothing had been brought forth up to now about the newness of divinity, just as it was not disputed, nor can it be retorted from the newness itself of each institution, that another divinity demonstrated by Christ is sufficient, when also this newness pronounced by the creator will have been established in Christ not to be wondered at, and it will have been necessary certainly to expound another God first, then to introduce his discipline, because God provides authority to discipline, not discipline to God; unless also Marcion learned plainly such perverse things not through a teacher of letters, but through letters a teacher.

choices.why: third-person singular imperfect active of destruere

pass_b_english: I will also address the Sabbath upfront: this dispute could never have arisen unless Christ carried the God of the Sabbath within him. After all, no one would have debated why he was destroying the Sabbath if he were actually supposed to destroy it. And he would have been obliged to destroy it only if it belonged to another god; in that case, no one would have been surprised to see him doing what fit that deity. They were astonished, therefore, precisely because it was unfitting for him to bear the Creator God and then assault that God's own Sabbath.

To settle the primary issues once and for all, so we do not keep encountering the same points in every argument the opponent builds on some new institution of Christ, this definition will stand: the dispute centered on the novelty of each institution because nothing had yet been produced about a novelty of divinity. Just as that question was never debated, neither can it be countered from the novelty of the institutions themselves that Christ has sufficiently demonstrated a different divinity. For when the Creator has pronounced that this very novelty is not to be wondered at in Christ, it becomes clear that one must first expound another God and only then introduce his discipline, since God confers authority on discipline, not discipline on God. Unless, of course, Marcion plainly learned such perversions not from a teacher through letters, but from letters through a teacher.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex conditional and causal structures of the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The distinction in the final clause regarding the teacher and letters is preserved. The title 'Christ and the Sabbath' correctly names the thought.

The Latin text is correctly translated, with accurate handling of terms like 'destrueret' as 'he was destroying' and 'nouitate institutionis cuiusque' as 'newness of each institution'. The citation to the Sabbath is preserved, and the theological distinctions are maintained. No errors in scripture citations or doctrinal content are found.
